props.title: What you can do before you decide anything

items.title: Ship a real page
items.description: Not a sandbox with fake data. The demo site is production code, and the page you edit is the page you deploy.

items.title: Use every widget
items.description: All 34, no locked sections, no watermark. Nothing is held back for a paid tier that does not exist.

items.title: Deploy it
items.description: To your own host, under your own domain, for a client, on day one. MIT means exactly that.

items.title: Leave
items.description: Delete the account and the code keeps working. That is the difference between a template and a platform.

items.title: What happens on day 14?
items.description: Nothing. There is no clock — this is the honest version of a trial page. If your product does expire, say the date, say what you keep, and say it here rather than in an email on day 13.

items.title: Do I need the account at all?
items.description: No. It syncs brand presets between machines; everything else works from the repository. A trial page that admits its signup is optional converts worse and retains far better.

items.title: Where does my data live?
items.description: EU region, deletable from the account page, and no analytics until you accept them. The compliance strip above is the short version your buyer’s IT reviewer will look for.
